summary.en: Move each unfinished maximum right with neighbour swaps and stop after a complete unchanged pass.
summary.bn: পাশাপাশি মান বদলে বড় মান ডানে পাঠাও, আর অদলবদল না হলে আগেই থামো।

notes: C17 baseline; general algorithm bounds treat input size as variable.

examples.title: Order five marks, including a tie
examples.explanationHtml: Four shrinking sweeps move the maxima right. Eight adjacent exchanges produce 1 3 3 5 7.

examples.title: Sort numbers entered at the keyboard
examples.explanationHtml: Bubble comparisons also order negative marks. The keyboard example ends at -2 -2 0 1 4 7.

examples.title: Use sorted neighbours to find distinct marks
examples.explanationHtml: After bubble ordering, only changes between neighbouring values start a new group. There are three distinct marks.

examples.title: Show one pass without claiming the whole array is sorted
examples.explanationHtml: One sweep leaves 3 5 3 1 7 after four swaps. The final 7 is correct, but the unfinished prefix still contains reversed neighbours.

practice.title: Count adjacent exchanges
practice.statementHtml: For bubble sort, read n (0..64) and n keys in -99..99 after displaying Enter n, then n values:. Apply strict adjacent swaps and early exit; report swaps = S, counting actual exchanges only.
hints: Increase the counter only inside the strict greater-than branch.

practice.title: Count complete bubble passes
practice.statementHtml: Measure complete sweeps in early-exit bubble sort. Print Enter n, then n values:, read a length 0..64 and that many integers (-99..99), then print passes = P. Include the final unchanged sweep if it runs; a singleton uses zero sweeps.
hints: A completed outer-loop iteration counts even when it performs no swaps.

practice.title: Explain the Bubble Sort invariant
practice.statementHtml: For Bubble Sort, state what stays true as the main process repeats. Explain the start, preservation and completed result.
hints: Use the changing boundaries and the processed region in this method.
practice.answerHtml:
During an inner pass, the value at the current right endpoint is the maximum of all values visited so far in that pass. Comparing it with the next value preserves this fact. Therefore the completed pass puts the unfinished prefix's maximum at its right edge. Before the next pass, the sorted suffix contains the largest already placed values.

Each pass extends that suffix by one, or stops because no inversions remain between neighbours. Either outcome makes progress. Swaps preserve the collection of values because each exchange moves two existing values without creating or deleting one. These arguments establish both ascending order and preservation of the input.

practice.title: Derive the resource cost of Bubble Sort
practice.statementHtml: Derive the shrinking-pair sum and explain what the early-exit flag changes on ascending input.
hints: Count the work from this algorithm rather than naming a class alone.
practice.answerHtml: Worst-case comparisons sum to (n - 1) + (n - 2) + ... + 1 = n(n - 1)/2. Reverse order also forces that many adjacent swaps when keys are distinct. Thus worst-case time is Θ(n²). Under the usual uniformly random permutation model, average work is also Θ(n²). Early exit reduces the best case to Θ(n), while auxiliary storage remains Θ(1).

quiz.prompt: After the first bubble pass on [7,3,5,3,1], where is 7?
quiz.explanation: The running maximum moves right at each adjacent comparison.

quiz.prompt: Why can a full swap-free bubble pass stop the algorithm?
options: All unfinished adjacent pairs are ordered
The first value must be zero
quiz.explanation: Together with the final suffix, adjacent order proves global order.

quiz.prompt: Which comparison keeps bubble sort stable?
quiz.explanation: Equal records must not exchange places.

quiz.prompt: How many comparisons does reverse-order bubble sort make for n distinct keys?
quiz.explanation: Each successive pass has one fewer unfinished pair.

options: At the start of each pass
quiz.explanation: Each sweep needs its own record of whether anything changed.

quiz.prompt: How far can the final minimum move left in one left-to-right pass?
options: All the way to index zero always
quiz.explanation: Earlier neighbour pairs have already been visited.

quiz.prompt: What is early-exit bubble sort best-case time on ascending input?
quiz.explanation: The algorithm still checks n - 1 adjacent pairs once.

quiz.prompt: Which array follows one complete bubble pass on [3,2,1]?
quiz.explanation: The largest 3 travels right, but the minimum moves left only once.

quiz.prompt: What does the swap flag become for an already ordered pair?
quiz.explanation: An ordered pair does not set the flag.

quiz.prompt: How many comparisons remain in pass = 2 for n = 5?
quiz.explanation: The unfinished prefix has two adjacent pairs to test.

keyPoints.en: Each pass finalises the largest unfinished value.
keyPoints.bn: প্রতি পাসে বাকি অংশের সবচেয়ে বড় মান ঠিক জায়গায় যায়।

keyPoints.en: A complete unchanged pass permits early exit.
keyPoints.bn: পুরো পাসে বদল না হলে আগেই থামা যায়।

keyPoints.en: The flag belongs to one pass at a time.
keyPoints.bn: প্রতিটি পাসে flag নতুন করে শুরু করো।
কঠোর তুলনা ব্যবহার করলে সমান key-এর ক্রম থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Worst-case work is quadratic with constant workspace.
keyPoints.bn: সবচেয়ে খারাপ ক্ষেত্রে কাজ quadratic, বাড়তি জায়গা constant।

examQuestions.question: Apply strict-swap bubble sort to [7,3,5,3,1]. Show the array after every complete pass and identify the newly final suffix value.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
StageStateDecision
Pass 1[3,5,3,1,7]Four swaps carry 7 to its final cell.
Pass 2[3,3,1,5,7]The remaining maximum 5 moves right.
Pass 3[3,1,3,5,7]The rightmost unfinished 3 becomes final.
Pass 4[1,3,3,5,7]The final reversed pair is repaired.
